title: Tenses Quiz 4
description: Show which of two past actions happened first.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the past perfect correctly?
options: When I arrived, the film had start.
When I arrived, the film has started.
When I arrived, the film was start.
When I arrived, the film had started.
questions.explanation: The film started before I arrived, so had + past participle is needed. Watch out: has started is a present tense.

questions.question: When we reached the station, the train {{1}} (leave).
questions.explanation: The train left first, so the earlier action is in the past perfect. Watch out: left alone would not show the order of events.

questions.question: 'She had eaten before he arrived.' Which happened first?
questions.explanation: The past perfect marks the earlier action. Watch out: the action in the past simple is the later one.

questions.question: The past perfect is formed with had + past participle.
questions.explanation: Had + past participle: she had left, they had finished. Watch out: had + base verb is wrong.

questions.question: 'She had wrote the letter' is correct.
questions.explanation: The past participle of write is written: She had written the letter. Watch out: wrote is the past simple form.

questions.question: By the time I got home, my sister {{1}} dinner. (already eat)
questions.explanation: Eating happened before I got home, so the past perfect is used. Watch out: eat has the past participle eaten, not ate.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I never had seen snow before I moved here.
I have never seen snow before I moved here.
I had never seen snow before I moved here.
I had never saw snow before I moved here.
questions.explanation: Seeing snow came before the move, so had + seen. Watch out: saw is the past simple, not the participle.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The past perfect often appears after said, when the loss came before the speaking.

questions.question: Which tense is 'They had been waiting for two hours'?
questions.explanation: Had been + -ing is the past perfect continuous. Watch out: it describes an action that went on until a past moment.

questions.question: I was tired because I {{1}} (work) all day.
questions.explanation: The tiredness is the result of the longer earlier action: had been + -ing. Watch out: had worked would not stress the duration.

questions.question: Match each form with its tense.
questions.explanation: Match the form to the name. Watch out: had alone is not enough; it needs the participle.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: When I arrived, she already left.
accepted: When I arrived, she had already left.
When I arrived, she had already left
When I arrived, she had left already.
When I arrived, she had left already
questions.explanation: She left before I arrived, so the past perfect is needed. Watch out: already belongs between had and the participle.
